Theme Name: Verification-before-trust is the dominant workflow signature
Draws From (Dimension/Theme): Operational Core (confidence via verification) + Text Mechanics (Verification, Native-Speaker Collaboration)
Claim: Across confidence, resource use, and process reflection alike, riddles are trusted not because of who wrote them but because they were checked by a relative, teammate, or AI before being finalized.
Relevance to Deliverables: Background context for write-up; not directly actionable for leads/contributors.

Theme Name: AI is consistently positioned as adversarial QA, not as an author
Draws From (Dimension/Theme): Text Mechanics (AI Feasibility Testing, GenAI Co-Augmentation)
Claim: AI's role is described the same way regardless of question - testing whether a model can solve/guess the riddle, with riddle authorship remaining human throughout.
Relevance to Deliverables: Useful for v0 reconciliation: check whether v0 riddles show evidence of this human-authorship-with-AI-QA pattern.

Theme Name: Broad-vs-local representativeness is an unresolved tension
Draws From (Dimension/Theme): Operational Core (Q3 commonality/regional split) + Wildcard Sourcing (niche vs ease) + Region Specificity Dimension
Claim: The dataset contains two different default philosophies for what "representative" means - broad/national vs. deep/local - and individual respondents pick one without reconciling it with the other.
Relevance to Deliverables: Strong candidate for "commonalities between culture teams" graphs - quantify the 3-way split (broad / niche / variable).

Theme Name: Team coordination friction is a real, recurring operational pain point
Draws From (Dimension/Theme): Operational Core (Asynchronous Collaboration, Accountability Metrics) + Project Reviews (Documentation Friction)
Claim: Independent of culture/language, multiple respondents flag the same operational gaps - async work, late-joining collaborators, unclear ownership, attribution issues.
Relevance to Deliverables: STRONGEST input for "feedback to riddle leads."

Theme Name: Effort/ease is not evenly distributed across the writing timeline
Draws From (Dimension/Theme): Text Mechanics (Lived Experience Anchoring -> Data-Generation Fatigue) + Wildcard Sourcing (Easy to Write)
Claim: Riddle-writing starts easy (memory-driven) and gets harder as easy material runs out; wildcard topic choice is sometimes driven by chasing remaining ease rather than deliberate design.
Relevance to Deliverables: STRONGEST input for "writing suggestions for new contributors": front-load topic variety, expect a difficulty cliff partway through.
